**3B.6 Research Note: Ali Khamenei (2024)**

**Bottom line:** I found no strong evidence that Khamenei reduced domestic fear and insecurity in a durable way. The dominant 2024 pattern is the opposite: coercive enforcement, executions, torture/abuse, and impunity. The only positive signals are discretionary pardons/commutations, which are too limited to count as a broader de-fear or de-securitization strategy.

| Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | QIDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| [Iran: Draconian campaign to enforce compulsory veiling laws through surveillance and mass car confiscations](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/03/iran-draconian-campaign-to-enforce-compulsory-veiling-laws-through-surveillance-and-mass-car-confiscations/) | Amnesty International | 2024-03-06 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/03/iran-draconian-campaign-to-enforce-compulsory-veiling-laws-through-surveillance-and-mass-car-confiscations/ | Authorities used surveillance, mass police checks, confiscations, prosecutions, flogging, prison terms, and “morality” classes to enforce veiling rules. This is strong evidence of a political fear climate built through routine coercion, not a reduction in insecurity. | 3B.6; also 3B.5, 3B.2 |
| [Iran executes 853 people in eight-year high amid relentless repression and renewed war on drugs](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/04/iran-executes-853-people-in-eight-year-high-amid-relentless-repression-and-renewed-war-on-drugs/) | Amnesty International | 2024-04-04 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/04/iran-executes-853-people-in-eight-year-high-amid-relentless-repression-and-renewed-war-on-drugs/ | Amnesty reported a major execution surge, including mass use of the death penalty after unfair Revolutionary Court trials. That supports a broader climate of fear, not protection from violence or insecurity. | 3B.6; also 3B.1, 3B.2 |
| [Iran security forces rape, torture detainees](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/04/22/iran-security-forces-rape-torture-detainees) | Human Rights Watch | 2024-04-22 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/04/22/iran-security-forces-rape-torture-detainees | HRW documented rape, torture, sexual assault, and coerced false confessions by security forces. This is direct evidence that coercive state violence was used in ways that would intensify fear rather than reduce it. | 3B.6; also 3B.1, 3B.2, 3B.4 |
| [Iran: Two years after ‘Woman Life Freedom’ uprising, impunity for crimes reigns supreme](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/09/iran-two-years-after-woman-life-freedom-uprising-impunity-for-crimes-reigns-supreme/) | Amnesty International | 2024-09-11 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/09/iran-two-years-after-woman-life-freedom-uprising-impunity-for-crimes-reigns-supreme/ | Amnesty said there were still no effective, impartial investigations into killings, torture, sexual violence, or disappearances, while families faced harassment and arbitrary detention. That points to sustained fear and retaliation, not lawful de-escalation. | 3B.6; also 3B.1, 3B.2, 3B.4 |
| [Iran will not impede IAEA access, head of its atomic organisation says](https://theprint.in/world/iran-will-not-impede-iaea-access-head-of-its-atomic-organisation-says/2403254/) | Reuters via ThePrint | 2024-12-14 | https://theprint.in/world/iran-will-not-impede-iaea-access-head-of-its-atomic-organisation-says/2403254/ | This is a limited positive signal of procedural openness in a narrow nuclear-oversight channel. It does not show a broader reduction in domestic fear or a change in the state’s coercive posture. | 3B.6; also 3B.4, 2B.10 |
| [Leader approves pardoning, commuting sentences of about 3,000 Iranian convicts](https://www.presstv.ir/Detail/2024/09/20/733636/Leader-approves-pardoning-convicts) | Press TV | 2024-09-20 | https://www.presstv.ir/Detail/2024/09/20/733636/Leader-approves-pardoning-convicts | Khamenei approved pardons or commutations for 2,887 convicts, including some security-related cases and minors. This is the strongest positive item I found, but it is episodic clemency, not a system that materially lowers domestic fear. | 3B.6; also 3B.1 |
| [Iran’s leader grants clemency to 2,654 inmates, including foreign nationals](https://english.news.cn/20240617/61af4b6135bc4f07bd0d76069a67ffe7/c.html) | Xinhua | 2024-06-17 | https://english.news.cn/20240617/61af4b6135bc4f07bd0d76069a67ffe7/c.html | Khamenei approved pardons or commutations for 2,654 inmates, including security-charge prisoners and foreign nationals. This is a limited mitigating act, but it is not evidence of a broader move away from fear-based governance. | 3B.6; also 3B.1 |
| [Iran: Security forces use deadly force against a woman during veiling enforcement, authorities still fail to investigate](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/09/iran-two-years-after-woman-life-freedom-uprising-impunity-for-crimes-reigns-supreme/) | Amnesty International | 2024-09-11 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/09/iran-two-years-after-woman-life-freedom-uprising-impunity-for-crimes-reigns-supreme/ | The same report also shows that enforcement pressure was still producing lethal and intimidating outcomes. That undercuts any claim that domestic insecurity was being reduced rather than reproduced by the state. | 3B.6; also 3B.1, 3B.2, 3B.5 |

**Search gap**
- I did not find reliable 2024 evidence of a sustained policy that reduced domestic fear without replacing it with state terror.
- The available positive material is limited to discretionary clemency and narrow procedural cooperation, not systemic protection from intimidation or abuse.
- I found no credible evidence of independent, rights-protective policing or a genuine de-escalation of the political fear climate.
